title: 浪淘沙（把酒祝东风）
titleEn: Waves Washing Sand (I Raise My Cup to the East Wind)
author: 欧阳修
intro: Walking with a friend among the flowers of Luoyang, the poet notices that this year’s blossoms are redder than last year’s — and wonders who he will be looking at next year’s with.
analysis: 这首词写和朋友在洛阳城东重游赏花。开头很有意思：词人举起酒杯向东风（春风）敬酒，请它慢一点，让大家从从容容地多玩一会儿。接着写地点：垂柳拂动的大道，正是去年两人手拉手游遍花丛的地方。下阕直接说出心里的遗憾：朋友相聚太难，分别太快，这种惆怅没有尽头。最后三句是全词最动人的地方：今年的花比去年开得更红，明年的花一定更好——可是明年还能和谁一起看呢？花一年比一年好，人却不一定还在一起，用“花”的越来越美来反衬“人”的聚散无常，这种写法叫“反衬”。语言平白，感情却很深。
analysisEn: This lyric records a walk with a friend through the flowers east of Luoyang. It begins with a charming gesture: the poet raises his cup to the east wind — the spring wind — and asks it to slow down so they can enjoy the day without hurrying. Then he names the place: the willow-lined road where, a year ago, the two of them walked hand in hand through every flowering grove. The second stanza says plainly what hurts: friends meet so rarely and part so quickly, and the regret never ends. The last lines are the heart of the poem. This year the flowers are redder than last year; next year they will be lovelier still — but who will be there to see them with him? The flowers keep getting better while the people may scatter. Setting the beauty of the flowers against the uncertainty of human meetings makes the sadness sharper, though every word is simple.
background: Ouyang Xiu (1007–1072) was a leading statesman, historian and essayist of the Northern Song. This lyric is thought to date from around 1032, when he was a young official in Luoyang; the friend is traditionally said to be the poet Mei Yaochen.
pronunciation: 谁 shuí（诗词中常读 shuí，口语也读 shéi）；处 chù；从容 cóng róng。

lines.py: bǎ jiǔ zhù dōng fēng, qiě gòng cóng róng
lines.lit: Holding wine, I toast the east wind: let us for now be unhurried together.
lines.en: I lift my cup to the east wind: stay a while, and let us take our time.

lines.py: chuí yáng zǐ mò luò chéng dōng
lines.lit: Drooping willows, the purple road, east of Luoyang city.
lines.en: Willows hang over the broad road east of Luoyang.

lines.zh: 总是当时携手处，游遍芳丛。
lines.rhythm: 总是/当时/携手处，游遍/芳丛
lines.py: zǒng shì dāng shí xié shǒu chù, yóu biàn fāng cóng
lines.lit: All are places where we held hands back then, roaming through every fragrant grove.
lines.en: Every step is where we once walked hand in hand, through grove after flowering grove.

lines.py: jù sàn kǔ cōng cōng, cǐ hèn wú qióng
lines.lit: Meeting and parting, painfully hurried; this regret has no end.
lines.en: We meet and part in such a hurry — and the ache of it never ends.

lines.py: jīn nián huā shèng qù nián hóng
lines.lit: This year’s flowers surpass last year’s in red.
lines.en: This year the flowers are redder than last year.

lines.zh: 可惜明年花更好，知与谁同？
lines.rhythm: 可惜/明年/花更好，知与/谁同
lines.py: kě xī míng nián huā gèng hǎo, zhī yǔ shuí tóng
lines.lit: Pity — next year the flowers will be even better; who knows with whom I’ll share them?
lines.en: Next year they will be finer still — and who will I be seeing them with?

words.en: to hold up a cup of wine
words.note: 把：拿着，现代汉语“把握”“把手”里还有这个意思。
这里是向东风祷告、敬酒，现代汉语“祝福”“祝酒”。
古义“暂且”，现代汉语“暂且”“姑且”。
现代汉语仍用，如“从容不迫”。
即垂柳，诗词里“杨”“柳”常通用。

words.en: the main road of the capital
words.note: 陌：路。古人称京城、大城市的道路为“紫陌”，今天不用。
即洛阳，北宋的“西京”，以牡丹出名。
现代汉语仍用，常比喻合作，如“携手共进”。
现代汉语说“相聚和分别”，成语“聚散无常”。
古诗里的“恨”多是遗憾、惆怅，比今天的“恨”（hate）轻得多。

imagery.name: 春风
imagery.zh: 词人向东风敬酒，请它留住春光——春风代表美好而短暂的相聚时光。
imagery.en: He toasts the spring wind and begs it to linger — it stands for a lovely season, and a meeting, that will not last.

imagery.name: 酒
imagery.zh: 举杯敬东风，是挽留时间的一个天真动作。
imagery.en: Raising a cup to the wind is an innocent attempt to hold time back.

imagery.name: 花
imagery.zh: 花一年比一年红，反衬人的聚散无常：花年年会开，朋友却不一定年年相伴。
imagery.en: The flowers grow redder each year, while friends may not be together next year — nature returns, people scatter.
